children: Ryanair Holdings Plc (EURONEXT:RYA) reported first-half FY27 profit down 15% to €2.15 billion as revenue rose 3% to €10.08 billion, cut its passenger target to 214 million and gave no full-year profit guidance. It declared an interim dividend of €0.273 per share and plans an €800 million buyback from February, subject to market conditions.
: Ryanair’s first-half FY27 profit fell 15% to €2.15 billion as revenue rose 3% to €10.08 billion. It cut its passenger target to 214 million and gave no FY27 profit guidance.
: Ryanair declared an interim dividend of €0.273 per share, payable in late February 2027, and plans an €800 million buyback from that month, lasting about 10 months, subject to market conditions.
: Ryanair has hedged 80% of FY27 fuel at about $67 a barrel and 25% of FY28 fuel at about $95. Current forward prices could add an estimated €2 billion to FY28 fuel costs.
: Ryanair Holdings Plc (RYA) said fares are rising meaningfully during a period when it typically stimulates prices. The airline has sold half of its third-quarter seats so far.
: Ryanair expects EASA to certify the Boeing 737 MAX 10 by December’s end. It plans to receive its first 16 jets in 2027, with deliveries possibly starting in January or early February.
: Ryanair (RYA) carried over 19.4 million passengers in October 2026, up 1% year over year, on 109,100-plus flights. Load factor held at 93%; trailing 12-month traffic rose 5% to 215.4 million.
: Ryanair Holdings Plc (RYA) is examining a pay freeze that would begin in April 2027.
: Ryanair is in advanced talks on engine-shop sites. Its CFO expects the first location to be announced by end-2026, with operations planned to start in late 2029.
